title: Freezer paper stencil transfer
subtitle: Ironing a waxy paper template onto fabric to act as a traced guide.
excerpt: Freezer paper has a plastic-coated side that sticks to fabric when ironed and peels off cleanly without leaving residue. Cut the design from the waxy paper, iron it to the fabric, and draw round the edge. The paper is repositionable and reusable several times.
sourceNotes: Freezer paper technique as applied to needlework and quilting, synthesised from contemporary practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A paper with a plastic coating on one side, originally used in food storage. The plastic side adheres temporarily to fabric when pressed with a warm iron. Used as a repositionable stencil or tracing guide in sewing and embroidery.

content.text: is inexpensive, easy to cut, and sticks firmly enough to trace around without shifting. Unlike iron-on transfers, the marks are made by you with a pen, so the design sits exactly where you place the template. The paper peels off cleanly and can be repositioned or reused.

items.name: Sharp scissors or craft knife for cutting the template

content.text: How to use a freezer paper template
Trace or print the design onto the dull (paper) side of the freezer paper.
Cut out the design shapes with scissors or a craft knife. For an outline transfer, cut out the inside of the design, leaving the outline edge intact as a stencil.
Position the template on the fabric, shiny side down.
Press with a dry iron on medium-low heat for five to ten seconds. The plastic coating will bond temporarily to the fabric.
Draw round the edge of the template with the water-soluble pen.
Peel the freezer paper away. Stitch the traced design, then rinse out the pen marks.

items.symptom: The paper doesn't adhere to the fabric
items.cause: The iron was too cool, or the shiny side was placed face up instead of face down.
items.fix: Check which side is shiny. Press for a longer count with the iron set slightly higher.

items.cause: The iron was too hot, melting the coating into the weave.
items.fix: Lower the iron temperature. Freezer paper needs only moderate heat to adhere.

content.text: Freezer paper templates are especially useful for repeated geometric shapes such as repeated leaf or petal motifs.
with freezer paper gives clean, repeatable outlines with no ink bleed.
